The dropped row's own name says it is the first half-pitch of Peking, same grade and first ascent party family; it is part of the 3-pitch Peking, not a separate climb. Stored rows only; not web-verified.
Peking is a 5.9 trad crack route (1969); Straight Outta' Peking is a 5.10d sport line from 2008 by different climbers.
Full Highway 97 (5.11d, 2 pitches) looks like the extension of Highway 97 (5.11b, 1 pitch); likely distinct climbs, area page would confirm.
The '(start)' row, 5.12a, appears to be the opening pitch of the 5-pitch 5.13a route; a topo/area listing would settle whether the catalog should hold it separately.
Pentameter Crack 5.6 (14 m) and Pentameter 5.9- (24 m) carry different map numbers (5a, 5b), grades and lengths.
Towards Interoception 5.7 (12 m) and Interoception 5.10a/b (24 m) carry different map numbers (8a, 8b), grades and lengths.
Wild Side Start 5.10a is the lower section, Wild Side 5.12c the full line; different grades; kept separate as a start variation.
Big Iron Direct is a direct variation of Big Iron; boulder variations conventionally count as separate problems despite the same stored grade.
Finish is a 5.10 finish with a dated first ascent; the main route is 5.11d with unknown FA; different grade and ascent.
Stevie Light V3- vs Stevie V6: different grades, a light/easy version beside the hard problem.
Chimney Face 5.11b vs Chimney Face Left 5.10b: different grades, left variant of the same face.
Full version is a 5.13d extension by a different climber (2003) of the 5.12a Spank the Monkey; separate pitch of climbing.
White Rabbit Buttress (top-rope 5.11+, 30 m) vs White Rabbit (trad 5.10b, no details); may be the same buttress but grade and style differ; the crag's area page would settle it.
Left Exit and Original Exit on the same V3 boulder are different exits; no description to merge on.
Get Lost V4 vs Get Lost Right V8-: different grade by four steps; separate lines.
Low Tides V2+ vs Low Tides Left V1+: left variation with a different grade.
Toilet bowl V2 stands alone; the Traverse (V1-2) is a described left-to-right sweep across the bowl.
Turtles back V2 vs Turtles Back Right (V3, also known by another name): different grade and a right-hand variant.
